title: Fast at the counter
question: Which firms have their jobs approved at the counter far more often than like jobs of the same cost and scope?
finding: Of 128,375 issued alterations with drawings filed 2012 to 2024, 86% were approved at the counter without full plan review: 67% of jobs costing $250,000 to $1 million and 62% of jobs of $1 million and over. 4 of 915 firms tested take the counter path far more often than like jobs of the same cost, kind of work and building use, year after year (10 points or more above like jobs, beyond 4.0 standard errors, in three quarters of active years); 45 are sent to full review far more often. Largest gap: Halyard Construction Inc., at the counter on 89% of 298 jobs where like jobs went there 76% of the time.
how: Issued alterations with drawings filed 2012 to 2024, leaving out Fire-only permits. Each job is set against jobs in the same cost band, filing year, kind of work (keywords in the permit description) and building use; cells under 30 are merged to three-year periods and then across building uses. The expected number at the counter for a firm is the sum of its cells' counter shares. A firm is listed when its counter share is at least 10 points above expectation, beyond 4.0 standard errors (set so that about 0.05 of the 915 firms tested would pass by luck), and above expectation in at least three quarters of its active years. Same floors as the speed test.
limits: The counter path is ordinary: most alterations take it. Which jobs may take it is set by the department's rules, which are not in the permit data; in the data it follows the kind of work far more than the cost (88% of tenant improvement or interior work jobs of $250,000 and over went to the counter, against 23% of addition or expansion jobs). The keyword control is crude, so a firm that only does one simple kind of job will sit above jobs that merely share a keyword with it. The records do not show who decided the path or why. A firm far above expectation is a place to ask whether its jobs were the kind the counter is for; it is not a finding that they were not.
